data.summary: Claude-labelled agent sends browser-protocol mouse events to an Etsy DataDome slider; immediate checks remain blocked
data.description:
A May 9, 2026 ClawBench V2 shopping recording labelled claude-opus-4-7 shows an agent encountering an Etsy anti-bot challenge and attempting to interact with its slider through the browser control protocol. This report documents an executed but unsuccessful circumvention attempt. It does not claim a successful or partial bypass, completed purchase, nonempty cart, account compromise, or access to protected data.

The initial Etsy navigation at source lines 3/4 returns DataDome-related content. Browser vision results at 5/6 and 9/10 describe a slider challenge, and a browser-target query at 7/8 identifies the CAPTCHA-delivery frame. The vision descriptions are tool interpretations, not independent screenshot verification.

The agent then sends nine browser-protocol mouse events at 11/12, 13/14, and 15/16-22: movement, press, six further movements, and release. Each request has its own matching tool result and reports local success without a tool error. These results establish that the browser tool accepted the input requests. They do not establish that Etsy trusted the input as human or that the challenge was passed. Mouse coordinates are omitted.

The immediately following snapshot at 23/24 still contains DataDome content. A later navigation to the Etsy homepage at 27/28 also returns that content. These observations show that the recorded gesture did not produce an immediate demonstrated clearance.

Later Etsy homepage and search responses at 42/43 and 46/47 show ordinary public site content and an empty-cart marker. The recording does not explain which transition enabled this access. It therefore does not establish that the earlier gesture caused challenge clearance. The final snapshot at 96/97 has generic cart-related context but no explicit nonempty-cart confirmation in the focused review. No cart addition or purchase is claimed.

The source is a controlled shopping evaluation, not evidence of a malicious or provider-operated campaign. The model label identifies the configured model; it does not establish that Anthropic operated the activity. The available browser tools and benchmark context may explain the agent's choice. No claim is made that the task prohibited challenge interaction.

Source: TIGER-Lab/ClawBenchV2Trace, immutable revision bb88da2b8a94044df7888d79c1ad4c7e88949043.

SHA256: 5398195225f78d4429930b2fdf24524f628f105595126dc9b0f4288928cc662e
Source quality: 52 tool calls, no malformed rows, and no non-single-result joins. The selected packet contains 18 calls and 18 results, including nine input events with unique IDs and local success. Packet SHA256: 121ef26ff3e07344d964c5077d7901cea78092ff9527e0ae2adc0b9125c9834d. The source hash was verified against the pinned repository on the owned research machine. The archived source was inspected as inert evidence. No target interaction was replayed.

The local evidence packet omits mouse coordinates, challenge URLs, account fixtures, arbitrary source prose, and executable scripts. Raw fixture-bearing transcripts are not attached. A signed-in duplicate search on 2026-10-16 returned zero matches for Etsy, DataDome, slider challenge, the exact task slug, the source hash, and a selected call ID. This bounded search excludes sensitive reports and attachment contents.

Finding #143 documents synthetic input against Zillow, and finding #183 documents failed BoardGameGeek verification attempts. This Etsy recording is a distinct target and trace. The tactic family is related, so global technique novelty is not claimed. Expert interest and acceptance remain unconfirmed.
